IL1RN ↔ GPR87 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.56 · pTM 0.69
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and topologically plausible as a secreted ligand (IL1RN, "Secreted to blood") meeting a plasma-membrane GPCR (GPR87). However, UniProt lists 3 glycosylation sites on GPR87, which on a GPCR must sit on the small extracellular face, the only surface IL1RN can reach. The supplied interface is very large (BSA 3577 Å2, 678 contacts), so it likely overlaps those unmodeled glycans, though no per-residue check was possible. The ipTM of 0.56 is only borderline, and GPR87 is annotated as a lipid (LPA) receptor, not a protein-ligand receptor.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: GPR87 is a Glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites, and IL1RN is a Glycoprotein with 1 site. On a GPCR these sites are extracellular, which is the only face a secreted ligand can contact, so they are plausibly at or near the large modeled interface. This was not verified per residue. The PubMed PTM searches (13 hits for IL1RN, 7 for GPR87) returned nothing specific to glycosylation of either protein. GPR87's documented ligand is the lipid LPA, which binds within the transmembrane bundle, not a protein.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers mentioning both IL1RN and GPR87.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction, and GPR87 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is genuinely unreported.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Map the three GPR87 glycosylation sites and the IL1RN site against the modeled interface residues, and confirm the interface uses only extracellular or transmembrane-boundary residues of GPR87. Re-fold with core glycans attached at the GPR87 sites. If the interface survives, test binding in the lab (e.g. IL1RN-Fc binding to GPR87-expressing cells, with IL1R1 as a positive control). The supplied minimum separation of 1.95 Å is tight, so also check the model for clashes.

WNT3 ↔ GPR101 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.55 · pTM 0.59
Rationale
WNT3 (secreted) and GPR101 (orphan plasma-membrane GPCR) are a compartment-plausible ligand/receptor pair with no hit in STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed, so it is novel. However, UniProt lists WNT3 as a Lipoprotein (1 lipidation site) and Glycoprotein (2 sites), and GPR101 also has 2 glycosylation sites; AF3's bare-sequence model at a borderline ipTM of 0.55 (interface pLDDT 67.7) represents none of these. WNT3's documented receptors are Frizzleds, and GPR101 is a class A GPCR, so the modeled interface is doubtful. No fold was run, so whether any modification site actually sits on the interface is unchecked.
PTM / glycosylation
WNT3 UniProt: Lipoprotein (1 lipidation site), Glycoprotein (2 glycosylation sites), 11 disulfide bonds. PubMed includes a paper reporting that N-glycosylation of Wnt3 regulates Wnt/β-catenin signalling (PMID 38994173). GPR101 UniProt: Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites; its PubMed PTM search returned nothing relevant. Both sets of modifications are on the extracellular side where a ligand-receptor interface would form, but whether they fall on the modeled contact residues was not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR101 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Re-fold with the WNT3 lipid and the N-glycans on both proteins represented, and check whether the interface survives and whether it sits on GPR101's extracellular face rather than spanning both sides of the membrane. Fold WNT3 against a Frizzled as a positive control and against unrelated class A GPCRs as a specificity control. If the interface persists, test experimentally with a binding assay or GPR101 signalling readout using lipidated WNT3.

Rationale
No prior record of this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, PubMed 0 hits), so it is novel, but nothing positively supports it. HPA has no subcellular or protein-level data for GPR146, HPA expression profiles show no shared enrichment, and the fold is borderline (ipTM 0.55, pTM 0.38, interface pLDDT 60.2, min separation 1.76 Å suggesting near-clashing contacts). NPR1 carries 7 annotated glycosylation sites and GPR146 one, and neither could be placed relative to the modeled interface, so the evidence does not reach CONFIRMED_NOVEL or a firm LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM call.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: NPR1 is a Glycoprotein with 7 glycosylation sites (extracellular ligand-binding domain) and 7 modified residues (phosphoprotein); GPR146 is a Glycoprotein with 1 site. The PubMed PTM search for NPR1 returned mostly plant and yeast NPR1 papers (uninformative); the GPR146 hits were not about its glycosylation. If the modeled interface involves NPR1's extracellular domain, glycans could occlude it; this was not resolved per residue.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR146 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is genuinely unreported.
Other subunits
NPR1 (second protomer; functional receptor is a homodimer, per general knowledge rather than a tool result);NPPA
Follow-up (not yet executed): Inspect which NPR1 region contacts GPR146 and confirm the interface is topologically consistent (not mixing extracellular and cytoplasmic residues). Check whether the 1.76 Å minimum separation reflects clashes. Re-fold with an NPR1 homodimer (with or without ANP/NPPA) plus GPR146 to see whether the contact survives or simply occupies the NPR1 dimer interface. Map NPR1's 7 N-glycosylation sites against the interface. If it holds up, test by co-IP or BRET in vascular or endothelial cells.

Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and both proteins are plasma-membrane proteins in the lymphoid/T-cell context, so a contact is topologically possible. However, ICAM1's ectodomain carries 8 UniProt N-glycosylation sites and GPR171 has 1, none of which AF3 modelled, and the ipTM of 0.55 is only borderline. I could not check whether any glycan site, or a mixed cytoplasmic/extracellular topology, falls on the modelled interface, so the artifact call is a caveat-driven lean rather than a demonstrated one.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists ICAM1 as a Glycoprotein with 8 glycosylation sites and 7 disulfide bonds; these sit on its Ig-domain ectodomain, the only region that could plausibly contact a GPCR's extracellular face. GPR171 is a Glycoprotein with 1 glycosylation site. The PubMed PTM search gave 1701 hits for ICAM1, but the top titles were generic inflammation papers and not informative; GPR171 gave 0. Whether any glycan site lies on the modelled interface was not checked per residue.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers mentioning ICAM1 and GPR171 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR171 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported.
Other subunits
ITGAL;ITGB2
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Map the modelled interface residues against ICAM1's N-glycosylation sites and against UniProt topology for both chains; discard the model if the interface mixes cytoplasmic and extracellular residues or is mediated by the TM helices. 2) Re-fold with core N-glycans attached on ICAM1 to see whether the interface survives. 3) Consider competition with ICAM1's established partner LFA-1 (ITGAL:ITGB2) and with GPR171's known ligand Big LEN (PCSK1N). 4) If the interface survives, test by co-IP or proximity assay in T cells.

C3 is a secreted plasma protein (HPA: secreted to blood) and GPR174 is a plasma-membrane GPCR on lymphocytes, so a ligand-receptor pairing is compartmentally plausible. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence all returned nothing, so the pair is novel. Confidence is low because ipTM 0.55 is only just above threshold (interface pLDDT 68.7, min PAE 9.1), the fold used the full-length C3 precursor rather than a physiological cleaved fragment, GPR174's established ligand is a lipid (LysoPS), and glycosylation sites on both proteins were not checked against the interface.
PTM / glycosylation
Both are glycoproteins per UniProt: C3 has 3 glycosylation sites, a thioester bond and extensive proteolytic processing; GPR174 has 2 glycosylation sites, location not returned. The PubMed PTM searches were non-specific. Whether any glycan sits on the modeled interface is unknown, so this is a caveat rather than grounds for an artifact call. The larger concern is that AF3 modeled the unprocessed C3 precursor, whereas the receptor-binding species in vivo are cleaved fragments (C3a, C3a-desArg, C3b and others).
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed co-mentions of C3 and GPR174.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no hit (GPR174 is not in its gene table, so that miss is uninformative). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. No prior report of this pair. UniProt lists C3AR1 and C5AR2 as the known GPCR receptors for C3 fragments, and LysoPS and CCL21 as GPR174 ligands.
Other subunits
C3AR1;C5AR2
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run in this triage. Other_subunits lists C3's known GPCR receptors as comparators, not missing complex members. Suggested next steps: (1) Re-fold GPR174 with individual C3 fragments (C3a anaphylatoxin, C3a-desArg, C3b/C3d) instead of the 1663-aa precursor, and check that the interface sits on GPR174's extracellular face or orthosteric bundle rather than its cytoplasmic loops. (2) Check whether GPR174's N-glycosylation sites fall at the interface. (3) Counter-screen C3a against related receptors (P2RY10, GPR34, C3AR1 as positive control) to test specificity. (4) Wet-lab: cAMP (Gs) assay in GPR174-expressing cells with purified C3a and C3.
Validation strategy: Stimulation assay (Compare full-length C3, C3b/iC3b/C3a/C3c/C3d fragments (and optionally PNGase F-deglycosylated C3) on GPR174-expressing vs GPR174-knockout cells, with LysoPS as a reference agonist.)
Why this method
C3 is a secreted plasma protein and GPR174 is a plasma-membrane GPCR on lymphocytes, so this is a paracrine/endocrine ligand-receptor pair. Cells need not co-express them, and a signalling readout tests function better than co-localization. GPR174 couples to Gs, so cAMP and pCREB are the plausible readouts.
Target tissue(s)
lymphoid tissue, liver
Why these tissues (HPA)
There is no real tissue overlap. C3 RNA is almost entirely liver (5062 nTPM, hepatocytes 5036 nCPM) and reaches the receptor through blood. GPR174 RNA is restricted to lymphoid tissue (15.7 nTPM), with the highest single-cell levels in T-cells (105 nCPM), NK-cells (76) and basophils (60). Lymphocytes are therefore the receptor-bearing side, bathed in plasma C3 (liver-derived).
Cell type(s)
T-cells, NK-cells, B-cells, Basophils, Thymocytes, Hepatocytes (C3 source)
Protocol notes
1) Use HEK293 (or CHO) cells stably expressing GPR174, with a CRE-luciferase or cAMP biosensor (GloSensor/HTRF cAMP). Use parental or empty-vector cells as the negative control. Confirm in primary human CD4+ T cells or Jurkat cells, with GPR174 knocked out by CRISPR, by measuring cAMP, pCREB (Ser133) and inhibition of TCR-induced proliferation or IL-2. 2) Treat with a dose range (1 nM–10 µM) of purified native human C3, C3b, iC3b, C3a, C3c and C3d, and with Hep G2 conditioned medium or co-culture as a physiological C3 source. Include a time course (5–60 min for cAMP, 4–6 h for the reporter). 3) Orthogonal binding check: use SPR or a cell-binding assay with tagged C3 on GPR174+ vs GPR174− cells, plus a β-arrestin recruitment assay (e.g. PathHunter) in case signalling is Gs-independent. 4) Run a glycosylation arm: PNGase F or Endo H pre-treated C3, and an N-glycan-site mutant of GPR174 if the interface overlaps a site. Test whether the response is lost, gained or unchanged.
Controls
Positive: LysoPS (the established GPR174 agonist), and forskolin for the maximal cAMP response. Negative: parental or GPR174-KO cells, heat-denatured C3, and an irrelevant plasma protein such as albumin at the same concentration. Specificity: C3a on C3AR1-expressing cells as a reference, and a C3AR1/C5AR2 co-expression arm to test whether the other subunits modulate the response. Also check LysoPS contamination, since lipid carry-over in plasma-derived C3 could give a false signal. Use delipidated C3 or recombinant C3.
Caveats
Confidence is low (ipTM 0.55, interface pLDDT 68.7, min PAE 9.1). The AF3 model used the uncleaved full-length C3 precursor, which does not exist in plasma, so the real binder may be a cleavage fragment (C3a, C3b, iC3b, C3d) or none. GPR174's known ligand is a lipid (LysoPS), so a peptide/protein interface is unprecedented. Plasma-purified C3 may carry lipids that activate GPR174 and give false positives. Glycosylation sites on C3 and GPR174 were not checked against the predicted interface, so a glycan could block or alter binding. GPR174 expression is modest (RNA only, no HPA protein data), and the C3AR1/C5AR2 co-subunits could confound the readouts. If no signal appears, consider that C3 may bind without activating (a modulator or antagonist), and follow up with co-IP or a binding assay.

ITGAL ↔ P2RY10 LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX low confidence ipTM 0.55 · pTM 0.47
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and both are lymphoid-enhanced plasma-membrane proteins, so a cis interaction on lymphocytes is plausible. However, ITGAL is an obligate heterodimer with ITGB2 (CellPhoneDB integrin_aLb2_complex; UniProt describes all functions as ITGAL/ITGB2), and ITGB2 was absent from the model, so the contact surface may be one that ITGB2 occupies in vivo. The AF3 signal is also marginal (ipTM 0.55, interface pLDDT 59.6, min separation 1.81 Å suggesting clashes), and both proteins are glycosylated (12 and 3 annotated sites).
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: ITGAL is a Glycoprotein with 12 annotated glycosylation sites on its ectodomain; P2RY10 is a Glycoprotein with 3 sites, on its extracellular regions. The PubMed PTM search returned 7 non-specific hits for ITGAL and 0 for P2RY10. With a buried surface of 2879 Å2 and 591 contacts, any ectodomain part of the interface could plausibly overlap a glycan site; this is unverified without per-residue interface data, so it is a secondary caveat.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (P2RY10 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is genuinely unreported.
Other subunits
ITGB2
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run here (no fold tool was available in this session). Next steps: (1) re-fold ITGAL + ITGB2 + P2RY10 and see whether the ITGAL–P2RY10 chain-pair ipTM stays at or above 0.5 and the interface avoids the ITGB2-binding surface; (2) inspect the interface topology, since a real cis interaction should be TM/TM or same-side, and any interface mixing cytoplasmic and extracellular residues is an artifact; (3) check whether ITGAL or P2RY10 N-glycosylation sites sit on the interface; (4) if it survives, test by co-IP or proximity ligation of LFA-1 and P2RY10 in primary T or B cells.

Support is weak, though: ipTM 0.54 is only just above the 0.5 threshold, interface pLDDT is about 71, and GPR141 is an orphan with no HPA localization data. The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing specific to an interface (C5AR1 40 generic hits, GPR141 1 unrelated hit). These modifications probably sit on the extracellular N-terminus/loops or cytoplasmic tail rather than a lateral TM-TM interface, but site positions were not checked against the modeled contacts, so this is an unresolved minor caveat, not grounds for an artifact call.

GNAI1;GNAO1
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Inspect the model to confirm the interface is a lateral TM-helix contact with both receptors in parallel topology; reject it if it is antiparallel or mixes extracellular with cytoplasmic residues. 2) Check whether the C5AR1 N-glycosylation site and the two GPR141 sites fall on the modeled interface. 3) Counter-screen for specificity by folding C5AR1 against a few unrelated class A GPCRs; similar ipTM of about 0.5 would indicate generic 7TM packing. 4) Test experimentally by BRET/FRET or co-IP in a myeloid line such as differentiated HL-60, and confirm both are co-expressed at the same neutrophil maturation stage. The listed G-alpha subunits are C5AR1's known coupling partners from UniProt, not evidence of a missing obligate subunit.
Validation strategy: PLA (co-localization) (with GPR141 knockdown/knockout and single-antibody controls; optionally a C5a-stimulated vs. unstimulated arm)
Why this method
Both are 7TM GPCRs expected in the same cell membrane, and the question is whether they sit in close proximity as a heterodimer. PLA tests this in situ in primary myeloid cells at endogenous expression levels. Neither protein is a secreted ligand, so a stimulation assay is not the primary fit.
Target tissue(s)
bone marrow, peripheral blood neutrophils (isolated), monocytes (isolated)
Why these tissues (HPA)
Bone marrow is the only tissue where both are reported. C5AR1 has very high protein intensity there, and GPR141 RNA is 24.5 nTPM. At single-cell level, C5AR1 is high in neutrophils (2004 nCPM) and monocytes (1283 nCPM), and GPR141 is detected in neutrophil progenitors (17.8 nCPM). The overlap is therefore the neutrophil lineage.
Cell type(s)
neutrophils, neutrophil progenitors (promyelocytes/myelocytes), monocytes
Protocol notes
1) Use bone marrow sections or cytospins of CD34+-derived, differentiating neutrophil-lineage cells (e.g. HL-60 or PLB-985 differentiated toward neutrophils, plus primary bone marrow cells). GPR141 expression is low and is likely restricted to progenitors, so sample the differentiation time course. 2) Use PLA with a validated anti-C5AR1 (e.g. mouse mAb) and an anti-GPR141 (rabbit). Validate the GPR141 antibody first by western blot or immunofluorescence on GPR141-overexpressing versus knockout cells, because it is an orphan with little antibody validation. Use mild fixation (4% PFA) and avoid permeabilisation that disrupts the membrane. 3) Quantify PLA puncta per cell by confocal microscopy and compare with the controls. Run a follow-up with HEK293 cells co-expressing tagged receptors (e.g. NanoBRET or co-IP) to confirm the specificity of the interaction. 4) Optionally test whether C5a changes the PLA signal and whether GPR141 modulates C5a-induced Gi signalling (cAMP, Ca2+ flux) given the GNAI1/GNAO1 partners.
Controls
Positive: C5AR1 with a known interactor or a known GPCR homodimer pair (e.g. C5AR1 with C5AR2, or CXCR4 with CXCR4) to show PLA works for GPCR dimers. Negative: single-primary-antibody PLA, GPR141 CRISPR KO or siRNA cells, C5AR1 with an unrelated abundant membrane protein (e.g. CD45), and C5AR1 with a non-myeloid GPCR that is not expressed in the same cells. Also a mixed-cell control: C5AR1-only and GPR141-only cells mixed together, which should give no PLA signal.
Caveats
Confidence is low: ipTM is 0.54, interface pLDDT is about 71, and AF3 may pack 7TM bundles together without a bilayer, so a non-specific association is possible. HPA lists the main location of C5AR1 as Golgi, which probably reflects antibody or biosynthetic-pool staining rather than its functional plasma-membrane location. GPR141 has no HPA localization or protein data and its RNA level is low, so the PLA signal may be near background and antibody specificity is the main risk. Overlap is in bone marrow neutrophil lineage cells only, and GPR141 appears restricted to progenitors, where C5AR1 may be lower. PLA detects proximity of about 40 nm, so crowded receptors in the same membrane can give false positives. Positive results need a second orthogonal method (co-IP or BRET).

GLG1 ↔ GPR75 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.54 · pTM 0.59
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and compartments are compatible, but both are glycoproteins (UniProt: GLG1 5 glycosylation sites plus sialic acid; GPR75 3 sites) and AF3 folded bare sequence at only borderline confidence (ipTM 0.54, interface pLDDT 62.6, min separation 1.89 Å). I could not run a fold to check whether any glycan site sits on the interface or which membrane side it falls on, so the artifact call is an inference, not a per-residue finding.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: GLG1 carries the Glycoprotein and Sialic acid keywords with 5 annotated glycosylation sites; GPR75 carries Glycoprotein with 3 sites. PubMed supports GLG1 glycan modification (FUT3-synthesised Lewis-a on GLG1; polysialylation and shedding of E-selectin ligand-1); the GPR75 PubMed hits were 20-HETE signalling papers, not PTM-specific. GLG1's stated function is binding E-selectin, a lectin, so its recognised binding mode is glycan-dependent. By inference, a 5550 Å2 interface with 1104 contacts must involve GLG1's large luminal domain, since its cytoplasmic tail is very short, and so would face GPR75's glycosylated extracellular side. Whether a glycan site actually lies on the modeled interface was not verified.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for GLG1 + GPR75.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is unreported. UniProt gives GPR75's activator as CCL5/RANTES, and GLG1's partners as fibroblast growth factor and E-selectin.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Map the AF3 interface residues against UniProt N-glycosylation sites and topology for Q92896 (GLG1) and O95800 (GPR75), and confirm the interface does not mix cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. 2) If a glycan site is on the interface, re-fold with the core N-glycans attached and see whether the interface survives. 3) Inspect the model for clashes (min separation 1.89 Å) and for a diffuse wrap-around interface, which the very large buried area with only moderate pLDDT suggests. 4) If the interface holds up, test by co-immunoprecipitation or proximity labelling in neuronal or retinal cells expressing GPR75.

RNASET2 ↔ GPR82 CONFIRMED_NOVEL VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.54 · pTM 0.7
Rationale
RNASET2 is a secreted protein (HPA: secreted to blood, immunity; UniProt: Secreted, Signal) and GPR82 is an orphan cell-membrane GPCR (UniProt), so a ligand-receptor pairing is compartment-plausible. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence all returned nothing, so the pair is novel. Confidence is low because ipTM is borderline (0.54), HPA has no subcellular data for either protein, and both carry N-glycosylation sites (RNASET2 3, GPR82 2) whose position relative to the modeled interface was not checked.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: RNASET2 is a glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites and 4 disulfide bonds; GPR82 is a glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites. PubMed PTM search: 8 hits for RNASET2 (mostly not about its own glycosylation; one on expression in CHO-S cells), 0 for GPR82. Neither protein's function text describes a glycan-mediated binding mechanism (RNASET2 is an RNA-cleaving enzyme). Whether any glycosylation site lies on the modeled interface is unknown; this is an unresolved caveat, not evidence of an artifact.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count = 0 for RNASET2 and GPR82.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: not found (GPR82 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. GPR82 is annotated "Orphan receptor" in UniProt. No prior report of this pair.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Map the interface residues against UniProt topology and the N-glycosylation sites of RNASET2 (3) and GPR82 (2); if a site is on the interface, re-fold with the glycan attached. 2) Confirm the interface is on GPR82's extracellular side and not touching cytoplasmic loops. 3) Counter-fold RNASET2 against unrelated class A GPCRs to test specificity, given the borderline ipTM of 0.54. 4) Wet-lab: test recombinant glycosylated RNASET2 binding and signalling on GPR82-expressing cells (e.g. macrophages/Kupffer cells).
Validation strategy: Stimulation assay (Compare WT RNASET2 vs catalytically dead RNASET2 (H65F/H69F) and, optionally, PNGase F/EndoH-deglycosylated or N-glycan site mutant RNASET2 to test glycan dependence of the interface.)
Why this method
RNASET2 is a secreted protein and GPR82 is an orphan cell-surface GPCR, so the natural test is whether recombinant RNASET2 activates GPR82-expressing cells. A functional readout also distinguishes true agonism from non-specific binding, which matters given the borderline ipTM of 0.54.
Target tissue(s)
lymphoid tissue, intestine, liver, endometrium
Why these tissues (HPA)
GPR82 RNA is highest in lymphoid tissue (6.5 nTPM) and intestine (2.5 nTPM), and its single-cell signal is in Kupffer cells (65.1 nCPM), so liver macrophages and lymphoid immune cells are the receptor-bearing side. RNASET2 is secreted to blood and is very high in endometrial luminal cells (742 nCPM). There is no clear tissue overlap, so this is a paracrine/endocrine pairing and is best tested by adding ligand to receptor-bearing cells (co-culture or recombinant protein).
Cell type(s)
Kupffer cells, Endometrial luminal cells, Lymphoid/immune cells (macrophages, T cells)
Protocol notes
1) Use HEK293 or CHO cells stably expressing tagged GPR82 (e.g. N-terminal HA/FLAG) and parental cells as a control. Add recombinant human RNASET2 (mammalian-expressed, glycosylated) at 1 nM–1 µM. Measure cAMP, because GPR82 is reported to be constitutively active and probably Gi/Gs-coupled (GloSensor or HTRF, with forskolin to detect Gi inhibition). Also run a β-arrestin recruitment assay (PathHunter/NanoBiT) and a Ca2+ flux assay with Gα16/Gqi5 co-expression. 2) Confirm binding with a cell-surface binding assay: tagged RNASET2 on GPR82+ vs parental cells by flow cytometry. 3) Confirm in a physiological system: stimulate primary human macrophages or Kupffer-like cells (or THP-1/PBMC-derived macrophages) with RNASET2, with and without GPR82 siRNA/CRISPR knockout, and read out cAMP or ERK phosphorylation. Alternatively co-culture with RNASET2-secreting endometrial epithelial cells such as Ishikawa cells, with RNASET2 knockdown. 4) Run the glycosylation arm: PNGase F-treated or N-glycan-site mutant RNASET2 against WT.
Controls
Positive: a known agonist or assay-validation ligand for a co-expressed control GPCR (e.g. forskolin for cAMP, or a known ligand of an unrelated receptor in the same cell background). Negative: parental cells lacking GPR82; an irrelevant secreted RNase (e.g. RNase A/RNASE T1) or heat-denatured RNASET2; a mock-transfected receptor such as another orphan GPCR (GPR84 or GPR34); buffer-only vehicle. Also include catalytically dead RNASET2 to separate RNase activity from receptor engagement.
Caveats
The ipTM of 0.54 is borderline, so the predicted interface is low confidence. Both proteins carry N-glycosylation sites (RNASET2 has 3, GPR82 has 2), and their position relative to the modeled interface has not been checked. The AF3 bare-sequence model could therefore be blocked or altered by glycans, so use glycosylated, mammalian-expressed recombinant protein and test the deglycosylated version. HPA has no subcellular data for either protein, and GPR82 has low RNA expression, so antibody availability is uncertain and native-cell responses may be small. GPR82 is orphan and constitutively active, so a ligand effect may be subtle (inverse agonism or modulation). RNASET2 also has RNase-dependent and independent activities, which could produce receptor-independent effects on cells. RNASET2 is annotated as both predicted intracellular and secreted, so confirm its secretion in the chosen cells.

ITGAM ↔ P2RY10 LIKELY_SUBCOMPLEX low confidence ipTM 0.54 · pTM 0.51
Rationale
ITGAM is an obligate heterodimer with ITGB2 (CellPhoneDB integrin_aMb2_complex), and ITGB2 was absent from the model, so the borderline fold (ipTM 0.54, interface pLDDT 61.7, min separation 1.79 Å) may be using surface that ITGB2 normally occupies. The pair is unreported (STRING none, CellPhoneDB none, PubMed 0), but it is not supported well enough to call novel: ITGAM carries 19 glycosylation sites, and the two proteins are enriched in different immune cell types.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: ITGAM is a glycoprotein with 19 annotated glycosylation sites and 10 disulfides on its ectodomain; P2RY10 is a glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites. The PubMed PTM search gave 24 hits for ITGAM (the titles shown are not glycosylation-specific) and 0 for P2RY10. Heavy N-glycosylation of the ITGAM ectodomain could plausibly occlude a large modeled extracellular interface; whether any site lies on the interface was not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for ITGAM + P2RY10.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction (P2RY10 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is unreported.
Other subunits
ITGB2
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run for this triage. Re-fold ITGAM + ITGB2 + P2RY10 and see whether the ITGAM–P2RY10 chain-pair ipTM stays at or above 0.5 with ITGB2 present. In that model, check the interface topology (it must not mix cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, or bury TM helices implausibly) and whether any of ITGAM's 19 or P2RY10's 3 N-glycosylation sites sit on the interface. The 1.79 Å minimum separation suggests clashes, so inspect the structure directly. A CORUM/STRING complex check would also help.

PTPRC ↔ GPR171 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.53 · pTM 0.53
Rationale
Both are plasma-membrane proteins of lymphoid cells (GPR171 is T/NK-cell enhanced; PTPRC/CD45 is pan-leukocyte), so a cis interaction on T cells is physically possible, and STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed (0 hits) show no prior report. However, CD45 carries 17 annotated glycosylation sites on its ectodomain, which AF3 did not model, and the fold is only borderline (ipTM 0.53, interface pLDDT 67.7, minimum interface PAE 9.83 Å) with a very large, diffuse interface (BSA 5835 Å2, 1054 contacts). I could not check which side of the membrane the interface sits on, so the glycan-artifact call is an inference, not a verified finding.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt PTPRC: Glycoprotein keyword, 17 glycosylation sites and 9 modified residues; its function text describes CLEC10A recognising Tn-antigen glycans on CD45, i.e. glycan-mediated ectodomain interactions. UniProt GPR171: Glycoprotein, 1 glycosylation site. The PubMed PTM search for PTPRC returned 33 hits, but the titles shown are unrelated to glycosylation; GPR171 returned 0. A 5835 Å2 interface that includes the CD45 ectodomain would very likely overlap glycan-occupied surface, but the per-residue interface location was not verified.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning PTPRC and GPR171 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR171 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel as far as these sources go.
Other subunits
CD22;BCR
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold tool was available in this session, so the interface side and glycan overlap remain untested. Next steps: (1) map the AF3 interface residues onto CD45 topology (ectodomain vs TM vs cytoplasmic phosphatase domains) and onto GPR171's faces, and reject the model if it touches both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues; (2) if the interface is on the ectodomain, re-fold with N-glycans at the CD45 sites and see whether it survives; (3) if it is cytoplasmic (phosphatase domains on the GPCR intracellular face), re-fold with only the CD45 cytoplasmic region plus GPR171 to see whether ipTM improves; (4) test by co-IP or proximity labelling in primary T cells. The CellPhoneDB complex BCR_CD45_CD22 is B-cell specific and is listed in other_subunits only for completeness; it is not a relevant missing subunit for a T-cell GPCR.

PPIA ↔ GPR82 INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE low confidence ipTM 0.53 · pTM 0.68
Rationale
The contradiction is valid. PPIA reached the confidence gate against 4 of 11 receptors (36%) in the screen, so the fold says more about PPIA than about GPR82. PPIA is an abundant, sticky hub protein with 195 known interactions. Nothing suggests a shared co-receptor mechanism. PPIA's known extracellular receptor is BSG/CD147, and that is a single-pass protein, not a GPCR family. This breadth is therefore more likely promiscuity than real biology. The borderline ipTM of 0.53 adds to that. The compartment argument (secreted PPIA, membrane GPR82, HPA plausibility "plausible") shows only that the two could meet. It does not show specificity. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed found no prior report (known_interaction_strength=none), so the pair is not already known. But I can no longer call it a confirmed novel interaction. GPR82 has 2 glycosylation sites and PPIA binds heparan sulfate, so glycans may matter at the interface. No fold-level structural analysis was run (fold_evidence_status=not_run), so none of this can be checked. I'm downgrading to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR82 is a glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites, likely on the extracellular face. PPIA binds heparan sulfate. No evidence of glycan-mediated binding for this pair, and interface overlap was not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for PPIA + GPR82.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING no association; CellPhoneDB no curated interaction (GPR82 not in table); PubMed co-occurrence 0 papers. Pair is not previously reported, but absence of prior evidence does not establish specificity.
Other subunits
BSG
Follow-up (not yet executed): Check PPIA's folds against the other 7 receptors in the panel and compare ipTM scores. Run a control with unrelated GPCRs or scrambled sequences. Run a per-residue interface analysis to see whether the interface is on the extracellular face and whether it overlaps the GPR82 glycosylation sites. Consider testing PPIA with BSG as a positive control.
Validation strategy: Stimulation assay (Include BSG/CD147-knockout or CD147-blocking antibody arm, and a PNGase F/tunicamycin arm to test GPR82 glycan role)
Why this method
PPIA is a secreted extracellular ligand (HPA: secreted to blood) and GPR82 is an orphan membrane GPCR, so the two do not need to be in the same cell. A functional readout (G-protein/β-arrestin signalling) on receptor-expressing cells tests whether PPIA actually engages GPR82, which a co-localisation read cannot show.
Target tissue(s)
lymphoid tissue, intestine, liver (Kupffer cells)
Why these tissues (HPA)
GPR82 RNA is enriched in lymphoid tissue (6.5 nTPM) and intestine (2.5 nTPM), and in Kupffer cells (65.1 nCPM). PPIA is highly expressed, e.g. 3194 nCPM in gastric progenitor cells, and circulates in blood, so intestinal epithelium can supply the ligand locally while lymphoid and Kupffer cells provide the receptor. The expression overlap is therefore paracrine rather than same-cell. Liver is named only for the Kupffer-cell single-cell signal.
Cell type(s)
Kupffer cells, Gastric progenitor cells, Lymphoid immune cells (macrophage/monocyte/T cell)
Protocol notes
1) Use HEK293 or CHO cells stably expressing tagged GPR82, with parental cells as the control. Optionally add a monocyte/macrophage line or primary Kupffer-like macrophages with endogenous GPR82 (confirm by qPCR). Treat with recombinant human PPIA (1 nM–1 µM, 5–60 min). Read out cAMP (GPR82 is reported to be Gi/constitutively active, so use forskolin-stimulated cAMP), a β-arrestin recruitment assay (e.g. PathHunter/NanoBiT), and pERK. Use a GPR82-orphan-compatible Gα16 or Gqi5 chimera calcium flux as a secondary readout. 2) Test dependence on BSG: use BSG-KO cells or an anti-CD147 blocking antibody, and add BSG co-expression, since the pair is flagged with BSG as another subunit. Also test whether PPIA binding is blocked by cyclosporin A, which occupies the PPIA active site. 3) As orthogonal binding evidence, run flow cytometry or a cell-surface binding assay with tagged PPIA on GPR82-expressing versus parental cells, and run a pull-down with PPIA on membrane preparations.
Controls
Positive: a known GPCR agonist in the assay system (e.g. forskolin for the cAMP window; PPIA on CD147-expressing cells for the known PPIA–BSG pathway, e.g. ERK activation or chemotaxis). Negative: parental or empty-vector cells; heat-denatured PPIA or a PPIA catalytic-dead mutant (R55A); an unrelated cyclophilin (PPIB) or another secreted protein; an unrelated GPCR expressed at equal surface levels; pertussis toxin to test Gi dependence.
Caveats
Confidence is low (ipTM 0.53). PPIA is an abundant hub protein with 195 known interactions, so a hit could be nonspecific or act through its known receptor BSG/CD147 rather than GPR82 directly. HPA gives no subcellular data for either protein, and I could not check which side of the membrane the modeled interface sits on, or whether GPR82 N-glycosylation sites fall on the interface. If a glycan blocks the interface, the bare-sequence AF3 model would not match reality, hence the deglycosylation/glycosylation-site mutant arm. GPR82 RNA is low in bulk tissue (2.5–6.5 nTPM) and there is no protein-level HPA data, so a recombinant overexpression system is needed. Surface expression of tagged GPR82 and the lack of a validated antibody should be confirmed. Endogenous PPIA in conditioned medium may mask the response, so wash the cells or use serum-free medium.

Rationale
CCL28 is a secreted chemokine (UniProt: binds CCR3/CCR10) and GPRC5A is an orphan class C GPCR with HPA plasma-membrane localisation, so a secreted-ligand/surface-receptor pairing is compartment-plausible. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence all returned nothing, so the pair is novel. Confidence is low because the AF3 ipTM of 0.53 is only just above threshold, chemokines can dock generically into GPCR bundles, and one N-glycosylation site on each protein has not been checked against the interface.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists both as Glycoprotein with one glycosylation site each; GPRC5A also has 6 modified residues (Phosphoprotein keyword). The PubMed PTM searches returned only non-specific hits (biomarker and cancer papers), nothing on glycosylation of either protein. The GPRC5A glycosylation site may lie in its extracellular region and could sit near a chemokine-binding surface, but its position relative to the modeled interface was not checked (no fold or per-residue tool was available). A single glycan on each side is a caveat, not enough for an artifact call.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0 for CCL28 and GPRC5A.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPRC5A is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. No prior report of this pair; UniProt lists GPRC5A as an orphan receptor and CCL28's known receptors as CCR3 and CCR10.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Check whether the GPRC5A and CCL28 glycosylation sites fall on the modeled interface, and re-fold with the glycan attached if so. 2) Inspect whether the CCL28 contacts are on GPRC5A's extracellular face/TM bundle rather than its cytoplasmic side. 3) Specificity counter-screen: fold CCL28 against CCR10 (positive control) and unrelated GPCRs, and fold GPRC5A against other chemokines, to rule out generic chemokine-GPCR docking. 4) Wet-lab: test CCL28 binding or signalling (calcium flux, beta-arrestin) in GPRC5A-expressing lung epithelial cells.
Validation strategy: Stimulation assay (Include a binding arm: biotinylated or tagged recombinant CCL28 on GPRC5A-overexpressing vs. knockout cells (flow cytometry), plus an optional PNGase F / N-glycan site mutant arm for GPRC5A and CCL28.)
Why this method
CCL28 is a secreted chemokine (secreted to blood) and GPRC5A is an orphan class C GPCR, so the pair is a ligand/receptor candidate. HPA shows the two proteins expressed in different tissues, which fits a paracrine stimulation assay with recombinant ligand better than in situ proximity. A functional readout also tests whether binding does anything, which matters because chemokines can dock non-specifically into GPCR bundles.
Target tissue(s)
lung, urinary bladder, salivary gland
Why these tissues (HPA)
HPA shows GPRC5A RNA enriched in lung (190 nTPM) and urinary bladder (122 nTPM), with lung protein detected. CCL28 RNA is enriched in salivary gland (283 nTPM), and in salivary and lacrimal acinar cells (about 1260 and 1400 nCPM). The two proteins have no real tissue overlap: the receptor-bearing side is lung/bladder epithelium and the ligand-producing side is salivary/lacrimal acinar cells. Because CCL28 is secreted to blood and mucosal fluids, it can plausibly reach lung epithelium, so use recombinant CCL28 or salivary-acinar-conditioned medium on lung epithelial cells.
Cell type(s)
Lung epithelial cells (alveolar type II / bronchial epithelial), Urothelial cells, Salivary acinar cells (ligand source), Lacrimal acinar cells (ligand source)
Protocol notes
1) Use a GPRC5A-high lung epithelial line (e.g. BEAS-2B, or A549 if expression is confirmed by qPCR/WB) and a CRISPR GPRC5A-KO isogenic line. Also use HEK293 cells with and without GPRC5A overexpression. Confirm that CCR3/CCR10 are low or absent, or block them with antagonists or knock them out, so the response is not read through the known CCL28 receptors. 2) Stimulate with recombinant human CCL28 (10–500 nM dose-response, 5–60 min). Read out Gi/cAMP (forskolin-induced cAMP, or a BRET sensor), ERK1/2 and Src-family/STAT3 phosphorylation by western or AlphaLISA, β-arrestin recruitment (NanoBiT/Tango), and receptor internalization. GPRC5A localises to vesicles, so image its trafficking after stimulation. Also run a transwell migration assay as a functional readout. 3) Run a direct binding arm: tagged CCL28 on GPRC5A+ vs. KO cells by flow cytometry. Add a competition arm with excess untagged CCL28 and a heparin/GAG-stripping control, because CCL28 is highly basic and sticks non-specifically to cell-surface GAGs. 4) For the glycan check, treat cells or ligand with PNGase F, or mutate the predicted N-glycosylation sites on GPRC5A and CCL28 (N→Q), and compare the response with wild type.
Controls
Positive: CCL28 on CCR10- or CCR3-expressing cells (e.g. CCR10-transfected cells, with Ca2+ flux or migration readout), which confirms the ligand is active. Negative: GPRC5A-KO or parental cells lacking GPRC5A, heat-denatured CCL28, an irrelevant chemokine (e.g. CCL21) and a different class C GPCR (e.g. GPRC5B). Also use a CCL28 binding-interface mutant if the AF3 model suggests one, and pertussis toxin to test Gi dependence.
Caveats
Low confidence: the AF3 ipTM of 0.53 is borderline, and chemokines often dock non-specifically into GPCR bundles. CCL28 is very basic and binds cell-surface GAGs, so binding must be tested against GAG-stripped and KO controls. HPA lists GPRC5A mainly in vesicles (and also as predicted intracellular), so surface exposure is uncertain and the extracellular accessibility of the modeled interface needs confirming (surface biotinylation or non-permeabilized staining). GPRC5A is an orphan receptor with weak canonical G-protein coupling, so the signalling readout may be negative even if binding occurs. One N-glycosylation site on each protein has not been checked against the interface, so a glycan could block the AF3 bare-sequence interface. The glycosidase/mutant arm addresses this. HPA shows no tissue overlap of the two proteins, so any physiological relevance would be endocrine or paracrine, via mucosal secretion or blood.

ICOSLG ↔ GPR34 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.52 · pTM 0.59
Rationale
No prior evidence for this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB no match, PubMed 0 hits), and compartments/expression are compatible, so it is novel and not implausible. But ipTM is borderline (0.52), and UniProt lists both as glycoproteins with 5 glycosylation sites each, which the bare-sequence AF3 model does not represent. GPR34 is a lysophosphatidylserine (lipid) GPCR with no known protein ligand, and the large interface (BSA 2816 Å2, 648 contacts) may be transmembrane-helix packing made without a bilayer; I could not check where the interface falls because no fold was run.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: ICOSLG has the Glycoprotein keyword and 5 glycosylation sites (on its Ig ectodomain, by my reading of the topology); GPR34 has the Glycoprotein keyword and 5 glycosylation sites (on its extracellular N-terminus/loops, likewise inferred). The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing relevant (ICOSLG 1 unrelated hit; GPR34 8 hits on pharmacology and lymphoma). Any extracellular interface would likely involve glycosylated regions on both sides, but whether a site sits on the modeled interface was not verified.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction match (GPR34 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel as far as these sources go.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Inspect the AF3 model to see whether the interface is transmembrane-helix packing or ectodomain contact, and whether it mixes cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. Map the UniProt N-glycosylation sites of both proteins onto the interface, and if any land on it, re-fold with glycans attached. Canonical ICOSLG–ICOS binding and LysoPS–GPR34 binding are the expected real interactions; a wet-lab test (co-immunoprecipitation or a cell-surface binding assay in macrophages) is needed before pursuing this pair.

MST1 ↔ GPR37 CONFIRMED_NOVEL VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.52 · pTM 0.55
Rationale
HPA classes MST1 (macrophage stimulating 1) as secreted to blood and GPR37 as a membrane GPCR, so a ligand-receptor pairing is topologically plausible, and STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all returned no hit for the pair. Confidence is low because the AF3 ipTM of 0.52 is only just above the 0.5 threshold, the supplied p_twoway is 0.050, and the glycosylation caveat on GPR37 could not be checked against the interface. The MST1 UniProt lookup returned the wrong protein (STK4, the Hippo kinase aliased "MST1", Q13043), so no valid UniProt mechanism or PTM data was obtained for the MST1 side.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR37: UniProt lists the Glycoprotein keyword and 3 glycosylation sites, and the extracellular side is where a secreted ligand would bind, so a glycan at the modelled interface is possible but was not verified. MST1: uniprot_annotation returned STK4 (Q13043), not the macrophage stimulating protein, so its PTM data does not apply; the pubmed_ptm_glycosylation hits for MST1 (406) are likewise dominated by STK4/Hippo papers and are uninformative. No per-residue interface check was done, so there is not enough to call LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits. The symbol "MST1" is ambiguous with STK4 in the literature, so even a nonzero count would have needed disambiguation.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: not found. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. No evidence anywhere of a known interaction. UniProt lists prosaposin, osteocalcin and neuroprotectin D1 as GPR37 ligands; MST1 is not among them.
Other subunits
MST1R
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Re-pull UniProt for the correct MST1 protein (macrophage stimulating protein, P26927 from background knowledge) to get its glycosylation sites and domain structure. 2) MST1R (RON) is listed under other_subunits from background knowledge as the established MST1 receptor, not from any tool result; fold MST1–MST1R as a positive-control benchmark for the 0.52 ipTM. 3) Check whether the modelled interface falls on GPR37's extracellular N-terminus or loops rather than cytoplasmic residues, and whether any of the 3 GPR37 N-glycosylation sites sit on it; if so, re-fold with the glycan attached. 4) Test binding and signalling experimentally, e.g. MST1-induced ERK phosphorylation or internalisation in GPR37-expressing cells, with prosaposin as a positive control.
Validation strategy: Stimulation assay (Include MST1R-null/MST1R-blocked arm and a GPR37 vs vector-only arm to separate direct GPR37 signalling from MST1R-mediated effects)
Why this method
MST1 (HGF-like protein, MSP) is a secreted-to-blood ligand and GPR37 is a GPCR, so this is an endocrine ligand-receptor pair with no expected same-cell co-expression. A functional readout in receptor-expressing cells fits better than PLA. Because MST1R is named as another subunit, the assay must separate GPR37 effects from canonical MST1R signalling.
Target tissue(s)
liver, brain, retina
Why these tissues (HPA)
MST1 RNA is almost exclusively hepatic (liver 864 nTPM; hepatocytes 369 nCPM). GPR37 is in brain (67 nTPM; cerebral cortex protein intensity ~1.08M) and retina (36 nTPM). There is no real tissue overlap, so this would be endocrine signalling from liver to CNS/retina. Test it with recombinant MST1 on GPR37-expressing cells, not in a shared tissue.
Cell type(s)
Hepatocytes (MST1 source), Oligodendrocytes (GPR37+), Müller glia (GPR37+)
Protocol notes
1) Receptor cells: HEK293 or CHO cells stably expressing GPR37 (with and without MST1R), plus a vector-only control. Also test primary oligodendrocyte precursors or Müller glia/oligodendrocyte-lineage lines, which express GPR37 endogenously. 2) Stimulate with recombinant human MST1 (active, two-chain form, ~1–500 nM dose-response; 5–60 min). Active MST1 needs proteolytic cleavage, so compare pro-MST1 with the cleaved form, or use conditioned medium from HepG2 or hepatocytes. 3) Readouts: cAMP (GloSensor), β-arrestin recruitment (PathHunter/BRET), Ca2+ flux, and pERK1/2 and pAKT by western blot. Use MST1R signalling (pERK, pMET-like phosphorylation) as a reference. 4) Confirm binding orthogonally with a cell-surface binding assay (tagged MST1 on GPR37 cells, flow cytometry) or by co-IP/pulldown. Use an MST1R siRNA or blocking antibody to dissect dependence.
Controls
Positive: MST1 on MST1R-expressing cells (e.g. macrophages or MST1R-HEK) gives pERK/pRON. For GPR37, use the known ligands prosaposin/prosaptide (TX14(A)) or head activator. Negative: untransfected or vector-only cells, heat-inactivated MST1, an unrelated HGF-family protein (HGF), and a GPR37L1-expressing line for specificity. Verify GPR37 surface expression, for example with an N-terminal tag.
Caveats
Low confidence: ipTM 0.52, p_twoway 0.050, and the pair has no support in STRING, CellPhoneDB or the literature. The GPR37 N-terminus is heavily glycosylated, and the glycosylation could not be checked against the interface. GPR37 also misfolds and is retained intracellularly (HPA lists nuclear membrane), so surface expression in heterologous cells may be poor. The MST1 UniProt lookup returned STK4 (Q13043), so MST1 has no valid PTM or mechanism data. MST1 is also activated by proteolytic cleavage, which the AF3 model may not reflect. Any response could come via MST1R, so the MST1R arms are needed to interpret it. Tissue separation means any in vivo relevance would be endocrine and would have to cross the blood-brain or blood-retina barrier.

  "function": "Stress-activated, pro-apoptotic kinase which, following caspase-cleavage, enters the nucleus and induces chromatin condensation followed by internucleosomal DNA fragmentation (PubMed:11278283, PubMed:11517310, PubMed:15109305, PubMed:16510573, PubMed:8702870, PubMed:8816758). Key component of the Hippo signaling pathway which plays a pivotal role in organ size control and tumor suppression by restricting proliferation and promoting apoptosis (PubMed:11278283, PubMed:11517310, PubMed:15109305, PubMed:16510573, PubMed:8702870, PubMed:8816758). The core of this pathway is composed of a kinase cascade wherein STK3/MST2 and STK4/MST1, in complex with its regulatory protein SAV1, phosphorylates and activates LATS1/2 in complex with its regulatory protein MOB1, which in turn phosphorylates and inactivates YAP1 oncoprotein and WWTR1/TAZ (PubMed:16930133). Phosphorylation of YAP1 by LATS2 inhibits its translocation into the nucleus to regulate cellular genes important for cell proliferation, cell death, and cell migration (PubMed:16930133). STK3/MST2 and STK4/MST1 are required to repress proliferation of mature hepatocytes, to prevent activation of facultative adult liver stem cells (oval cells), and to inhibit tumor formation (By similarity). Phosphorylates 'Ser-14' of histone H2B (H2BS14ph) during apoptosis (PubMed:12757711). Phosphorylates FOXO3 upon oxidative stress, which results in its nuclear translocation and cell death initiation (PubMed:16751106). Phosphorylates FOXO1 on 'Ser-212' and regulates its activation and stimulates transcription of PMAIP1 in a FOXO1-dependent manner (PubMed:21245099). Phosphorylates SIRT1 and inhibits SIRT1-mediated p53/TP53 deacetylation, thereby promoting p53/TP53 dependent transcription and apoptosis upon DNA damage (PubMed:21212262). Acts as an inhibitor of PKB/AKT1 (PubMed:17932490). Phosphorylates AR on 'Ser-650' and suppresses its activity by intersecting with PKB/AKT1 signaling and antagonizing formation of AR-chromatin complexes (PubMed:21512132). CHRNE ↔ GPRC5A IMPLAUSIBLE medium confidence ipTM 0.52 · pTM 0.61
Rationale
No database or literature support (STRING and CellPhoneDB misses, 0 PubMed co-mentions) and no overlap in HPA tissue enrichment (CHRNE heart muscle/pituitary; GPRC5A lung/urinary bladder). CHRNE is an obligate subunit of the muscle nAChR pentamer (CHRNA1/CHRNB1/CHRND per CellPhoneDB), so folding it alone exposes inter-subunit surfaces that are buried in vivo; a borderline ipTM of 0.52 between two multi-pass membrane proteins most likely reflects non-specific helix packing. The pair is novel, but the evidence does not support it as a real interaction.
PTM / glycosylation
Both are UniProt glycoproteins (CHRNE 2 glycosylation sites, GPRC5A 1 site plus 6 modified residues). The PubMed PTM searches returned only unrelated disease and cancer papers. Whether any glycosylation site lies on the modeled interface was not checked; this is a secondary concern behind the missing subunits and lack of coexpression.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed co-mentions.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction; GPRC5A is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported.
Other subunits
CHRNA1;CHRNB1;CHRND
Follow-up (not yet executed): If pursued, check where the modeled GPRC5A contact sits on CHRNE: if it falls on surfaces that CHRNA1/CHRND occupy in the assembled (α1)2β1δε pentamer, it is an artifact of folding an isolated subunit. Also check interface topology for mixed cytoplasmic/extracellular contacts, and whether GPRC5A is expressed in skeletal muscle or at the neuromuscular junction at all. No fold was run for this candidate.

PLXNB3 ↔ GPRC5A IMPLAUSIBLE low confidence ipTM 0.52 · pTM 0.47
Rationale
The check says HPA gives no route for these two to meet. Neither protein is secreted, so contact would need them in the same place, and HPA shows zero shared protein-level tissue (PLXNB3 in brain/glia, GPRC5A in lung/bladder). Both are plasma-membrane proteins, so there is no compartment mismatch. That only makes a meeting possible in principle, and nothing observed supports it. The data also give no positive evidence: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all returned nothing for this pair (known_interaction_strength=none), and the AF3 model was marginal (ipTM 0.52, interface pLDDT 60.2, minimum interface PAE 10.46 Å). The flagged fold status is "not_run", so there is no separate structural result to weigh. PLXNB3's 8 glycosylation sites are unrepresented in AF3, which weakens the model further. I am moving from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to IMPLAUSIBLE because the absence of shared tissue combined with the weak model leaves no substantiated reason to expect these proteins to interact. Confidence stays low because HPA tissue data are coarse and low-level co-expression in some cells cannot be ruled out.
PTM / glycosylation
PLXNB3 has 8 glycosylation sites that AF3 does not represent. GPRC5A has 1 glycosylation site. Whether any lie on the interface was not checked per residue.

PubMed co-mention count is 0 for PLXNB3 and GPRC5A.

TLR8 ↔ P2RY8 IMPLAUSIBLE low confidence ipTM 0.52 · pTM 0.66
Rationale
UniProt places TLR8 in the endosome (an ssRNA sensor that homodimerises) and P2RY8 at the cell membrane (a GPCR for the metabolite GGG), so the two do not share a compartment by annotation. TLR8's ectodomain carries 21 annotated N-glycosylation sites that AF3 did not model, and the ipTM of 0.52 is only just at threshold. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed (0 hits) give no supporting evidence; this is novel but not well supported rather than strictly ruled out, since HPA has no localisation data for either protein.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt annotates TLR8 as a glycoprotein with 21 glycosylation sites and 6 disulfide bonds; these sit on the luminal LRR ectodomain, which makes up most of the protein and is the likely modelled contact surface. P2RY8 is a glycoprotein with 2 sites. The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing specific to this interface. Whether any glycan site lies on the modelled interface was not checked, because no fold was run.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no hit (P2RY8 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is novel, with no literature support.
Other subunits
TLR8 (homodimer);MYD88;GNA13
Follow-up (not yet executed): Low priority. If pursued, map the AF3 interface residues onto TLR8 topology and its 21 N-glycosylation sites, checking whether the contact is on the luminal LRR domain and whether it mixes cytoplasmic and luminal residues. Then re-fold with glycans attached and with TLR8 as a homodimer. A co-immunoprecipitation or proximity-labelling experiment in monocytes would test co-localisation in endosomes directly.

CHL1 ↔ GPR6 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.51 · pTM 0.49
Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and compartment-plausible: both are brain-expressed, CHL1 is a secreted/membrane adhesion protein and GPR6 a plasma-membrane GPCR. However, UniProt lists both as glycoproteins (CHL1 10 glycosylation sites, GPR6 3 plus a palmitoylation site), which AF3's bare-sequence model omits, and the fold is only marginal (ipTM 0.51, interface pLDDT 64.7). Whether any glycan actually sits on the modeled interface was not checked, so the artifact call is a caveat rather than a demonstrated result.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: CHL1 carries the Glycoprotein keyword with 10 annotated glycosylation sites and 6 disulfide bonds; GPR6 is a Glycoprotein (3 sites) and a palmitoylated Lipoprotein (1 lipidation site). The pubmed_ptm_glycosylation hits were mostly off-target (plant CHL1/NRT1.1 papers; general GPR6 expression papers) and add little. The large modeled interface (BSA 2276 Å2, 307 contacts) on glycosylated proteins makes glycan interference plausible, but no per-residue check of glycan sites against the interface was done.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning CHL1 and GPR6 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction, and GPR6 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is genuinely unreported.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Map the AF3 interface residues against the UniProt N-glycosylation sites of CHL1 (O00533) and GPR6 (P46095), and against GPR6 membrane topology, to confirm the contact is purely extracellular and not glycan-occluded. If a glycan sits on the interface, re-fold with it attached. Given the marginal ipTM (0.51), an orthogonal binding assay is needed before pursuing this pair, for example soluble CHL1 ectodomain on GPR6-expressing cells with a cAMP readout, since GPR6 is constitutively active and its proposed agonists are lipids.

TNC ↔ GPR75 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.51 · pTM 0.39
Rationale
The pair is compartment-plausible (TNC secreted to the extracellular matrix, GPR75 a plasma-membrane GPCR) and has no hit in STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed, so it is novel. However, TNC is a heavily glycosylated proteoglycan (24 UniProt glycosylation sites) and GPR75 carries 3 glycosylation sites, none of which AF3 modeled. The supplied fold metrics are also weak: ipTM 0.51 is borderline, interface pLDDT is 57.7, min separation of 1.55 Å indicates clashes, and a 7229 Å2 interface with 1587 contacts is implausibly large for a GPCR's small ectodomain, so it probably spans transmembrane or cytoplasmic regions a secreted protein cannot reach.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt annotates TNC as Glycoprotein and Proteoglycan with 24 glycosylation sites and 42 disulfide bonds, and GPR75 as Glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites. Both sets of glycans are on the extracellular surfaces where any real contact would occur, so they are plausibly relevant to the modeled interface. The PubMed PTM searches (134 hits for TNC, 11 for GPR75) returned nothing specific to glycosylation. No per-residue check of glycan sites against the interface was done.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers co-mention TNC and GPR75.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel. UniProt lists integrins (alpha-8/beta-1, alpha-9/beta-1, alpha-V/beta-3, alpha-V/beta-6) as TNC's receptors and CCL5 as GPR75's activating ligand.
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run here. Re-fold a truncated construct (individual TNC domains such as the FN-III repeats or fibrinogen globe against GPR75) rather than the 2741-token full complex. Then check the interface topology (extracellular only versus transmembrane/cytoplasmic) and whether the N-glycan sites on GPR75's N-terminus and extracellular loops, or on TNC, fall on the interface. If a confident extracellular interface survives (chain-pair ipTM above 0.5, no clashes), re-fold with glycans attached before any wet-lab binding assay.

B2M ↔ GPR82 CONFIRMED_NOVEL VALIDATE low confidence ipTM 0.51 · pTM 0.67
Rationale
No prior record of this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, PubMed co-occurrence 0), and a secreted protein (B2M, "Secreted to blood") against a plasma-membrane orphan GPCR (GPR82, UniProt "Cell membrane") is compartment-compatible. Support is weak, though: ipTM 0.51 is right at the threshold, with interface pLDDT 64.9 and min PAE 9.3 A. Which side of GPR82 the interface sits on, and whether its glycosylation sites are in it, was not checked, and B2M normally exists bound to MHC-I-like heavy chains.
PTM / glycosylation
GPR82: UniProt Glycoprotein keyword with 2 glycosylation sites, which could lie on the modeled contact surface if they are on the extracellular face; their positions and location relative to the interface were not checked. PubMed PTM search for GPR82 returned 0 hits. B2M: UniProt lists 7 "Glycosylation" features alongside the "Glycation" keyword; I read these as non-enzymatic glycation sites rather than structural N-glycans (my interpretation, not stated by the tool), so less likely to block an interface. The 27 PubMed hits for B2M looked unrelated to PTMs from the titles shown. Overall an unresolved caveat, not enough to call a PTM artifact.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for B2M with GPR82.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no curated interaction; GPR82 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. Nothing indicates this pair is already known.
Other subunits
FCGRT;CD1B
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run for this candidate (the fold tool was not available in this session), so the structural questions remain open. (1) Check that the B2M-contacting GPR82 residues are extracellular rather than cytoplasmic or mixed. (2) Check whether GPR82's two glycosylation sites fall in the interface, and re-fold with glycans if so. (3) Counter-screen B2M against a few unrelated GPCRs, since B2M is an Ig-domain hub (95 known interactions in HPA) and may co-fold non-specifically. (4) Test whether the GPR82-binding surface on B2M overlaps the surface it uses to bind MHC-I, FcRn (FCGRT) or CD1 heavy chains (CellPhoneDB lists FCGRT and CD1B; MHC-I is from UniProt); if so, only free B2M could bind. (5) Wet-lab test of binding of free B2M to GPR82-expressing cells.
Validation strategy: PLA (co-localization) (Include a B2M-knockdown/exogenous recombinant B2M add-back arm and a heavy-chain (HLA-ABC) co-stain to distinguish free B2M from MHC-I-bound B2M)
Why this method
B2M is ubiquitously expressed on cell surfaces and also circulates, while GPR82 is a plasma-membrane orphan GPCR with no known ligand, so there is no established signalling readout. PLA detects surface proximity in situ. A ligand-style stimulation assay is not suitable because there is no validated GPR82 readout, and orphan GPCR coupling is uncertain.
Target tissue(s)
Lymphoid tissue (spleen, lymph node, tonsil), Liver (Kupffer cells), Intestine (colon/small intestine)
Why these tissues (HPA)
GPR82 RNA is highest in lymphoid tissue (6.5 nTPM) and intestine (2.5 nTPM). Its single-cell expression is enriched in Kupffer cells (65.1 nCPM). B2M is secreted to blood and is also on the plasma membrane of nearly all nucleated cells, so it overlaps wherever GPR82 is present. HPA gives no tissue-specific B2M numbers, so this overlap is inferred from B2M's broad expression.
Cell type(s)
Kupffer cells, Lymphoid tissue immune cells (macrophages, T cells)
Protocol notes
1) Use non-permeabilized or mildly fixed cells and sections so that only surface or extracellular epitopes are probed. Run Duolink PLA with a mouse anti-B2M antibody and a rabbit anti-GPR82 antibody, after checking that the GPR82 antibody works. Check it on HEK293 cells overexpressing tagged GPR82 against parental cells, because GPCR antibodies are often poor. 2) Use HEK293 cells expressing epitope-tagged GPR82 (e.g. HA-GPR82) as a clean system, and run PLA with anti-tag plus anti-B2M. Test the effect of adding recombinant B2M. 3) Counter-stain with anti-HLA-ABC and anti-FCGRT or anti-CD1B. Test whether the PLA signal depends on MHC-I heavy chains, using B2M-null cells with B2M reconstituted. 4) Quantify PLA puncta per cell by confocal imaging in at least 3 biological replicates. If PLA is positive, confirm by co-IP of tagged GPR82 and B2M.
Controls
Positive: a known surface pair, such as B2M with HLA-A/HLA-B heavy chain, in the same cells (PLA positive control). Negative: single-antibody PLA controls, GPR82-knockout or parental HEK293 cells (no GPR82), an unrelated tagged GPCR with B2M, and a B2M-knockout line. An isotype-matched antibody control is also needed.
Caveats
Confidence is low: ipTM is 0.51, interface pLDDT is 64.9 and min PAE is 9.3 Å. B2M is nearly always bound to MHC-I-like heavy chains, so a positive PLA signal may reflect nearby MHC-I (a bystander, or an indirect link) instead of a direct B2M–GPR82 contact. It was not checked whether the GPR82 interface is extracellular or lies in a transmembrane or intracellular region, or whether it includes N-glycosylation sites, so it may be inaccessible or glycan-shielded. HPA gives no GPR82 subcellular or protein-level data, and the RNA is low except in Kupffer cells. GPR82 antibody quality is a main risk. PLA only shows proximity of about 40 nm, not a direct interaction or functional effect.

Rationale
No prior evidence links this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, 0 PubMed co-mentions), and expression/compartment do not rule it out. However, IGF2R's documented binding mechanism is lectin-type (mannose-6-phosphate recognition) and its ectodomain carries 18 annotated glycosylation sites, while GPR82 has 2 on its small extracellular surface; AF3's bare-sequence model represents none of this. The fold itself is also weak (ipTM 0.51 at the threshold, interface pLDDT 52.4, min separation 1.79 Å suggesting clashes), so the modeled interface is not trustworthy as drawn. I could not check whether any glycosylation site actually sits on the modeled interface, so the artifact call rests on general plausibility, not a per-residue finding.
PTM / glycosylation
IGF2R (UniProt P11717): Glycoprotein, Lipoprotein/Palmitate; 18 glycosylation sites, 59 disulfide bonds; function is binding phosphomannosyl (M6P) residues on lysosomal enzymes, i.e. a glycan-mediated mechanism. GPR82 (Q96P67): Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites. The PubMed PTM search gave 56 hits for IGF2R (the top titles are mostly not about PTMs) and 0 for GPR82. With about 2,832 Å² of buried surface on the heavily glycosylated IGF2R ectodomain, glycan interference at the modeled contact is plausible, but whether any site lies on the interface was not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning IGF2R and GPR82 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction found (GPR82 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported; GPR82 is an orphan receptor per UniProt.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Map the modeled interface residues against IGF2R's 18 and GPR82's 2 UniProt N-glycosylation sites, and check membrane topology of the interface (that it does not combine cytoplasmic and extracellular residues). Re-fold using only the relevant IGF2R domain repeats plus GPR82, with glycans attached, to see whether ipTM rises clearly above 0.5; the current 2,827-token fold with interface pLDDT 52 and 1.79 Å minimum separation is marginal. IGF2R has 116 known interactors (HPA), so a promiscuous or non-specific contact with a large ectodomain is also possible. If the interface survives, test by co-immunoprecipitation in macrophage/Kupffer-like cells.

Rationale
The check is right that HPA gives no shared protein-level tissue and that neither protein is secreted, so the data show no demonstrated route for contact. That lowers my confidence in the pair. It does not amount to the compartment mismatch that would justify IMPLAUSIBLE. Both CSPG4 and MRGPRF are plasma-membrane proteins, so they could in principle meet in cis or in trans on neighbouring cells. My earlier pull also showed single-cell RNA overlap in vascular smooth muscle cells and pericytes. That overlap is RNA-only and weaker than protein-level overlap. Missing protein-level overlap for an orphan GPCR such as MRGPRF is also weak evidence, because antibody coverage for GPCRs is poor. The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit), and no fold was run, so there is no structural support or structural refutation. The glycosylation concern (CSPG4 has 16 sites, MRGPRF has 1) is untested, and neither protein is a lectin. I therefore do not lean on it. Overall, the pair has no positive evidence for an interaction and no decisive evidence against one.
PTM / glycosylation
CSPG4 is a chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan with 16 glycosylation sites. MRGPRF has 1. No fold was run, so neither was checked against an interface. Neither protein is a lectin. The concern is hypothetical.
PubMed co-occurrence
pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for CSPG4 + MRGPRF.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence returned nothing for this pair (known_interaction_strength=none), so it is novel. MRGPRF is an orphan receptor.
Follow-up (not yet executed): Look for protein-level expression of MRGPRF in CSPG4-positive pericytes or smooth muscle cells. If that is supported, run an AF3 fold, including glycan-aware modelling for the CSPG4 ectodomain.

Rationale
The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit) and biologically possible: both are plasma-membrane proteins in lymphoid tissue. But the AF3 support is marginal (ipTM 0.5 exactly at threshold, partner pLDDT 51.7, min interface PAE 8.4 Å), and the 4153 Å2 interface is larger than GPR183's small extracellular surface would seem to allow, which suggests non-specific packing along the transmembrane bundle or a disordered tail. CD6's ectodomain carries 8 glycosylation sites that AF3 did not model, and I could not check whether any sit on the interface, so neither CONFIRMED_NOVEL nor LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM is justified.
PTM / glycosylation
CD6: UniProt keyword Glycoprotein with 8 glycosylation sites and 11 disulfides on the extracellular SRCR domains; it is also a phosphoprotein. The PubMed PTM search returned 37 hits, mostly about CD6 biology in general rather than specific modifications. GPR183: no annotated glycosylation, one modified residue; its natural ligand is an oxysterol in the transmembrane pocket. The CD6 ectodomain glycans could plausibly block an extracellular contact, but whether any lies on the modeled interface was not checked.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction (GPR183 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 papers. The pair is genuinely unreported. The documented partners are ALCAM/CD166 for CD6, and oxysterol 7α,25-OHC plus a CXCR5 heterodimer for GPR183.
Other subunits
ALCAM;CXCR5
Follow-up (not yet executed): No fold was run in this triage. Inspect the existing AF3 model for per-residue interface topology: whether contacts are CD6 ectodomain against GPR183 extracellular loops, TM against TM, or a physically impossible mix of cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. Check whether CD6's N-glycosylation sites fall on the interface, and re-fold with glycans if they do. If the interface is mostly CD6's TM helix or disordered cytoplasmic tail against the GPCR bundle, treat it as a likely artifact. ALCAM and CXCR5 are the known partners of each protein and could be used as comparison folds. If the model survives, test by co-immunoprecipitation or proximity assay (BRET/PLA) in primary T cells.

Guides B-cell movement along the B-cell zone-T-cell zone boundary and later to interfollicular and outer follicular regions (By similarity). Its specific expression during B-cell maturation helps position B-cells appropriately for mounting T-dependent antibody responses (By similarity). Collaborates with CXCR5 to mediate B-cell migration; probably by forming a heterodimer with CXCR5 that affects the interaction between of CXCL13 and CXCR5 (PubMed:22913878). Also acts as a chemotactic receptor for some T-cells upon binding to 7-alpha,25-OHC ligand (By similarity). Promotes follicular helper T (Tfh) cells differentiation by positioning activated T-cells at the follicle-T-zone interface, promoting contact of newly activated CD4 T-cells with activated dendritic cells and exposing them to Tfh-cell-promoting inducible costimulator (ICOS) ligand (By similarity). Expression in splenic dendritic cells is required for their homeostasis, localization and ability to induce B- and T-cell responses: GPR183 acts as a chemotactic receptor in dendritic cells that mediates the accumulation of CD4(+) dendritic cells in bridging channels (By similarity). Regulates migration of astrocytes and is involved in communication between astrocytes and macrophages (PubMed:25297897). Promotes osteoclast precursor migration to bone surfaces (By similarity). Signals constitutively through G(i)-alpha, but not G(s)-alpha or G(q)-alpha (PubMed:21673108, PubMed:25297897). Signals constitutively also via MAPK1/3 (ERK1/2) (By similarity)",

TFR2 ↔ GPR22 IMPLAUSIBLE low confidence ipTM 0.5 · pTM 0.67
Rationale
Both are integral membrane proteins (TFR2 single-pass type II, GPR22 a 7TM orphan GPCR), so a cis interaction needs the same cell, but HPA shows no overlap: TFR2 is liver-enriched (hepatocytes, erythrocyte progenitors) and GPR22 is in brain neurons and cardiomyocytes. The AF3 signal is borderline (ipTM 0.5, interface pLDDT 59.3, min separation 1.82 Å with 615 contacts and 3204 Å2 buried), which looks more like non-specific membrane-protein packing than a real interface. No STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed support exists; confidence is low because HPA has no localisation data for GPR22 and no fold was run to check interface topology.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt lists both as glycoproteins: TFR2 has 4 glycosylation sites on its ectodomain and GPR22 has 2. The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing specific to glycosylation of either protein at an interface. Glycans on the extracellular regions are an extra caveat for any modeled ectodomain contact, but the verdict does not rest on this.
PubMed co-occurrence
PubMed co-mention count is 0.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: no association found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction, and GPR22 is not in its gene table. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is unreported, but that novelty is not backed by biological plausibility.
Other subunits
TFRC;HFE;TF
Follow-up (not yet executed): Deprioritise. The other_subunits listed are TFR2's physiological partners from general knowledge (it is a homodimer that binds transferrin and HFE), not from a tool result; CellPhoneDB returned no complex for either protein. If the pair is revisited, inspect the model for which regions form the interface (TM helix against TM helix, or an interface mixing cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, would indicate an artifact) and check whether the TFR2 glycosylation sites sit on it. Any real co-expression would most plausibly be in cardiomyocytes or neurons, where TFR2 is low, and should be confirmed before any wet-lab work.

CTSG ↔ GPR34 LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM low confidence ipTM 0.5 · pTM 0.54
Rationale
No prior evidence for this pair (STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all empty), and a secreted neutrophil/mast-cell protease meeting a macrophage/microglia surface GPCR is compartmentally plausible. However, UniProt lists 5 N-glycosylation sites on GPR34 and 2 on CTSG, the only face CTSG can reach is GPR34's glycosylated extracellular side, and the fold is borderline (ipTM 0.5, interface pLDDT 63.3). No fold was run, so whether any glycan site actually sits on the modeled interface is unverified; this is a caveat-driven call, not a demonstrated artifact.
PTM / glycosylation
UniProt: GPR34 is a Glycoprotein with 5 annotated glycosylation sites; CTSG is a Glycoprotein with 2 sites. AF3 modeled neither. Site positions relative to the interface were not checked. The PubMed PTM searches (5 hits for CTSG, 8 for GPR34) returned nothing specifically about glycosylation of either protein.
PubMed co-occurrence
0 PubMed papers mention CTSG and GPR34 together.
STRING / CellPhoneDB
STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: not found. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel in the literature. Context from UniProt only: CTSG cleaves the receptors F2R/PAR1 and F2RL3/PAR4 and is a ligand for FPR1, so acting on a GPCR has precedent; GPR34's documented ligand is the lipid lysophosphatidylserine, not a protein.
Follow-up (not yet executed): 1) Fold the pair with structural analysis to see whether the interface falls on GPR34's extracellular N-terminus/loops and whether any annotated N-glycosylation site sits on it; if so, re-fold with the glycans attached. 2) Check the supplied geometry: 925 contacts, 3222 Å² buried area and a 1.93 Å minimum separation suggest an over-packed or clashing pose worth inspecting directly. 3) If the interface survives, test experimentally whether CTSG cleaves the GPR34 N-terminus (PAR-like) or modulates lysophosphatidylserine signalling in macrophages/microglia.
